title: SR-1.33 A test count that means behaviour
request: Closes G99: the seed-stage analysis (E1, E8). About a fifth of the test files read documents rather than run code: on main 5e1a1e05, 25 of 165 test files import nothing from src/ or bin/ and start no memev process, so the pass count overstates what is tested. The lab walk of every command (scripts/lab/cli-walk.sh) compares each command's exit code with an expected one that has gone stale, and nothing runs it. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: none.

tasks.title: Behaviour tests and document checks counted apart
requirements: a test file that only reads files (it calls no code from src/, bin/ or scripts/ and starts no process of them) lives under test/docs/; a test that runs repository code under src/, bin/ or scripts/ (test/docs-module-map.test.mjs runs scripts/docs/module-graph.mjs) is a behaviour test and stays in test/
npm test runs both and prints two lines, behaviour tests: N pass, M fail and document checks: N pass, M fail; CI's job summary shows both

scripts/test-kinds.mjs, run by npm test, fails naming the file when a test file outside test/docs/ neither calls code from src/, bin/ or scripts/ inside a test nor starts a process of it, or when a file under test/docs/ does either; importing a constant (such as PKG from ./helpers/tmp.mjs) or a module it never calls does not count
wherever the README or docs/DEVELOPING.md give a test count, it is the behaviour count
npm test exits non-zero when any behaviour test or document check fails, is cancelled or never runs, and when scripts/test-kinds.mjs fails; each count line comes from the run it reports

tasks.title: The lab walk runs and its expectations are current
requirements: scripts/lab/cli-walk.sh takes each command's expected exit code from docs/EXIT-CODES.md, a table of every command the walk runs, by the walk's id, with its documented exit code, and a --check mode runs the walk in a sandbox HOME with no network and exits non-zero naming each unexpected code
CI runs scripts/lab/cli-walk.sh --check on every pull request
every script under scripts/lab/ runs in CI in a check mode, or says at its top why it cannot run there
--check keeps every command away from the account-wide service managers and the tunnel programs by itself, whatever the caller's environment
the walk reports each unexpected code once, in both directions: a refusal that now succeeds is as unexpected as a success that now fails
